_meta.how_built: One entry per note, written by hand from the note text. The pipeline never infers these fields with an LLM. 'basis' records why each field was chosen so a reviewer can re-check it against the note.

fields.routes: Routes the note applies to, as 'Origin-Destination'. ['ALL'] means every route in the dataset.
fields.window_start: First date the effect applies (inclusive, ISO).
fields.window_end: Last date the effect applies (inclusive, ISO). null = open-ended / still in force.
fields.effect: increase | no_effect | decrease. Only 'increase' can ever justify a flag.
fields.max_effect_pct: Largest cost rise the note can plausibly explain. null = the note gives no figure (a sanity cap from config applies).
fields.summary: Short paraphrase used in template explanations.

notes.summary: highway flooding forced detours and raised trip costs on Chennai-Bangalore
notes.basis: Text: 'disrupted normal truck movement from Feb 24 to Mar 8 ... higher trip costs. Roads were passable again by Mar 9.' Window ends Mar 8, so the week of 2025-03-10 is outside it. No % given.

notes.summary: a regional festival week brought a temporary transporter surcharge on Ahmedabad-Mumbai
notes.basis: Dated 2025-01-20 (a Monday), describes 'a regional festival week' -> that Monday-Sunday week only. 'temporary surcharge' -> increase. No % given.

notes.summary: a nationwide diesel price rise pushed costs up roughly 5-7% on all routes
notes.basis: 'Diesel prices rose nationwide starting this week ... across all routes by roughly 5-7%.' Starts 2025-05-05, no end given -> open-ended. Upper bound 7%. Because it hits every route, it cannot explain one route rising above its peers.

notes.summary: a new toll plaza opened on a highway stretch not used by any route in this dataset
notes.basis: 'the affected routes are not part of this dataset' -> no effect on any route here.

notes.summary: highway maintenance caused minor delays between Mumbai and Delhi without significantly affecting costs
notes.basis: 'minor delays for about a week; costs were not significantly affected.' -> one week, no effect.

notes.summary: an industry report said freight demand stayed stable with no major disruptions
notes.basis: Dated 2025-09-22, 'this quarter' -> Q3 2025. 'stable ... no major disruptions' is evidence against a cost rise.

notes.summary: road conditions on Delhi-Jaipur improved after resurfacing
notes.basis: Improved road conditions after resurfacing -> if anything lowers cost; persists, so open-ended. Can never justify a rise.

notes.summary: no significant disruptions on Kolkata-Bhubaneswar; freight moved normally
notes.basis: Dated 2025-06-09, 'this quarter' -> Q2 2025. Explicitly no disruption.

notes.summary: Chennai-Bangalore returned to normal conditions after flood repairs
notes.basis: Confirms a return to normal -> evidence costs should NOT be elevated. Trap: same route as N001 but it explains nothing about a rise.

notes.summary: a new vehicle tracking mandate's compliance costs were absorbed by transporters without a rate change
notes.basis: 'absorbed by transporters without a rate change' -> explicitly no effect on freight rates.
